candidate_results.text:
# Introduction to Artificial Intelligence

## Purpose

This document provides an overview of Artificial Intelligence and explains how AI systems are used to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence.

## Requirements

AI systems generally require data, algorithms, computational resources, and a suitable problem definition.

## Process

An AI system processes available data, applies predefined algorithms or learned patterns, and produces an output based on the input.

## Applications

Artificial Intelligence is commonly used in recommendation systems, virtual assistants, image recognition, fraud detection, and automated decision-support systems.

## Responsibilities

Teams working with AI systems should ensure that the system is properly tested, documented, and used for its intended purpose.

# AI Data Preprocessing

## Purpose

This document explains the importance of preprocessing data before using it for Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning systems.

## Requirements

Raw data should be collected from reliable sources and inspected for missing values, duplicates, incorrect formats, and inconsistent information.

## Process

The preprocessing workflow may include data cleaning, duplicate removal, missing-value handling, normalization, transformation, and feature preparation.

## Quality Checks

Data should be checked for completeness, consistency, correctness, and compatibility with the selected AI model.

## Responsibilities

Data and AI teams are responsible for maintaining clean datasets, documenting preprocessing operations, and ensuring that changes to preprocessing logic are properly tested.

# Generative AI

## Purpose

This document provides an overview of Generative AI systems that create new content from learned patterns.

## Requirements

Generative AI systems require training data, model architectures, computational resources, and suitable evaluation methods.

## Process

A trained model receives an input prompt or condition and generates content based on patterns learned during training.

## Applications

Generative AI is used for text generation, image generation, coding assistance, summarization, and conversational applications.

## Responsibilities

Teams should evaluate output quality, reliability, safety, and appropriate usage boundaries.

# Computer Vision

## Purpose

This document describes Computer Vision and explains how AI systems analyze and interpret images and videos.

## Requirements

Computer Vision applications require image or video data, preprocessing methods, suitable models, and computational resources.

## Process

Input images are first prepared through preprocessing operations. A trained model then identifies patterns, objects, features, or other visual information.

## Applications

Computer Vision is used in object detection, facial recognition, medical image analysis, quality inspection, autonomous systems, and image classification.

## Responsibilities

Teams should verify image quality, evaluate model accuracy, and consider variations in lighting, camera position, image resolution, and other environmental factors.

# Deep Learning

## Purpose

This document explains the basic concept of Deep Learning and the use of neural networks for solving complex AI problems.

## Requirements

Deep Learning projects generally require large datasets, neural network architectures, training algorithms, and sufficient computational resources.

## Process

Data is provided to a neural network during training. The model calculates predictions, compares them with expected results, calculates an error, and updates its parameters to improve future predictions.

## Applications

Deep Learning is widely used in speech recognition, computer vision, natural language processing, recommendation systems, and generative AI.

## Responsibilities

Developers should monitor training performance, prevent overfitting where possible, evaluate the trained model, and maintain reproducible training configurations.

# Natural Language Processing

## Purpose

This document explains Natural Language Processing and its role in enabling computers to process and understand human language.

## Requirements

NLP systems require text data, preprocessing techniques, language representations, and suitable machine learning or deep learning models.

## Process

Text is commonly cleaned and tokenized before being converted into numerical representations. The processed data is then provided to an NLP model for analysis or prediction.

## Applications

NLP is used for sentiment analysis, text classification, machine translation, question answering, summarization, and chatbots.

## Responsibilities

NLP developers should validate the quality of text processing and ensure that the model performs appropriately for the intended language and use case.

# Classification

## Purpose

This document explains classification as a machine learning task for predicting discrete categories.

## Requirements

Classification requires labeled examples, input features, target classes, and evaluation metrics.

## Process

A model learns patterns from labeled examples and assigns an input to one of the defined classes.

## Applications

Classification is used in spam detection, document categorization, fraud detection, and sentiment analysis.

## Responsibilities

Developers should evaluate class-specific performance and consider class imbalance when interpreting results.

# Reinforcement Learning

## Purpose

This document explains reinforcement learning and how agents learn through interaction with an environment.

## Requirements

Reinforcement Learning requires an environment, an agent, states, actions, rewards, and a learning strategy.

## Process

The agent observes the current state, selects an action, receives a reward, and updates its policy based on the experience.

## Applications

Reinforcement Learning is used in robotics, game playing, recommendation systems, resource allocation, and autonomous decision-making.

## Responsibilities

Teams should define suitable reward functions, monitor training behavior, and evaluate whether the learned policy performs safely and effectively.

# Supervised Learning

## Purpose

This document explains supervised learning using labeled training examples.

## Requirements

Supervised learning requires labeled data, input features, target values, an algorithm, and an evaluation method.

## Process

The algorithm learns relationships between input features and known target values and uses them to make predictions.

## Applications

Supervised learning is used for classification, regression, forecasting, and many prediction tasks.

## Responsibilities

Developers should select appropriate evaluation metrics and ensure that training and evaluation data are properly separated.

# Machine Learning Fundamentals

## Purpose

This document explains the fundamental concepts of Machine Learning and how machines learn patterns from data.

## Requirements

A Machine Learning project requires relevant data, appropriate features, a learning algorithm, and an evaluation method.

## Process

The process generally includes collecting data, preprocessing the data, selecting features, training a model, evaluating its performance, and improving the model when required.

## Model Evaluation

Models can be evaluated using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, mean squared error, or other problem-specific measurements.

## Responsibilities

This document provides an overview of Artificial Intelligence and explains how AI systems are used to perform tasks that normally require human intelligence.

AI systems generally require data, algorithms, computational resources, and a suitable problem definition.

## Process

An AI system processes available data, applies predefined algorithms or learned patterns, and produces an output based on the input.

## Applications

Artificial Intelligence is commonly used in recommendation systems, virtual assistants, image recognition, fraud detection, and automated decision-support systems.

## Responsibilities

Teams working with AI systems should ensure that the system is properly tested, documented, and used for its intended purpose.
